description: Issue #787: the reporter-position Heritage-alias path reaching the user procedure's NO-OUTPUT guard, EXECUTED. `define forward … print 1 … end` is a COMMAND — it never reaches `return` — so using it as a reporter via `print fd` is `ol-no-output` (`spec/execution-model.md:346-349`). Fixtured separately from its two siblings because this diagnostic carries `params.procedure`, a DIFFERENT param name from the arity diagnostics' `params.callable`, and params on this path are exactly what this saga has gotten wrong five times (#670 `operation`, #733/#734 `callable`, #737/#747 and #741/#762 `keyword`): asserting one param name leaves the other unpinned, which is the M4 audit's F3 finding — an unasserted field is an unprotected one. The value is the CANONICAL `"forward"`, byte-identical to what `print forward` reports, never the surface `"fd"`; the `source_span` still covers the two columns of `fd` the learner wrote, so canonicalizing the param did not canonicalize the span. Note the event stream is NOT empty: the procedure genuinely runs — `procedure-enter`, its own `print 1`, then `procedure-exit` with `result: null` — and only then does the reporter position reject the absent value, which is what distinguishes this from the arity fixture, where the call is rejected before the body ever runs. Before the fix this program raised a raw host `TypeError` instead, exactly like its siblings. `"execute": true` because `execute()` runs `parse()` only and never `check()`. TRANSITIONAL FIXTURE (ruling #833, slice #839): like both siblings, this needs a user procedure registered under a Heritage alias's canonical name, and every one of the thirteen canonicals is a built-in name that #833 rules may never be registered — so once #839 lands, `define forward` halts at phase 1 and this stops being expressible as source→events. See `heritage-reporter-alias-reaches-canonical-user-procedure` for why the production fix is nonetheless not transitional, and for the request to carry these regressions forward as lower-level evaluator tests rather than deleting them.

diagnostics.message: forward doesn't report a value here — it never reaches return.
